source_title: Finalized authoritative structured areas are mutable, unsigned and outside correction lineage
source_evidence: Migration 0128 defines `session_block_areas` as the authoritative ordered area/laterality rows and explicitly grants authenticated studio members SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE under an `FOR ALL` membership policy. The finalization trigger list predates this table and does not guard it. The signed snapshot does not include it, and the correction dispatcher has no structured-area target.
source_failure_scenario: After finalization, a practitioner—or any authenticated member able to call PostgREST—deletes “left cheek” and inserts “right cheek,” or removes all areas. The finalized status and original signed hash remain unchanged. No correction version preserves or restores the prior authoritative rows.
source_affected: Finalized treatment records, treated-area history, laterality, practitioner trust, exports and any future decision support derived from those rows.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated membership in the same studio and knowledge of a block identifier; no owner role or special service credential is required.
source_test_limitations: Migration-shape/source tests can prove the policy text but do not prove immutability. Existing finalization tests cannot cover a table that was added later unless explicitly updated.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fresh-DB test: finalize a record, then assert direct insert/update/delete and area-replacement RPC all fail; assert a reasoned correction creates immutable before/after versions; assert snapshot hash changes when area/laterality/order changes.
source_recommended_fix: Emergency containment migration: attach a finalized-parent guard to `session_block_areas`; revoke direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from `authenticated`; permit mutations only through a validated draft-only command. Add structured areas to canonical snapshot v2 and correction/amendment support. Run a production-safe audit query for post-finalization area mutations before enabling or expanding use.
source_rollout_considerations: Forward-only migration. First contain writes, then introduce snapshot v2/correction support. Do not rewrite historical signed snapshots silently; version the snapshot schema and record any remediation as an attributed correction.

source_title: Finalization can race a child write and sign a state different from the committed finalized rows
source_evidence: Child-table write guards perform a plain parent-status SELECT. The finalizer locks only the session row, builds the snapshot, hashes it and inserts finalization artifacts. It does not lock every child row/table or force child mutations through a lock-compatible command.
source_failure_scenario: Transaction A begins an update while the session is draft and its trigger observes draft status. Transaction B locks the session, snapshots children and finalizes. Transaction A then commits the already-authorized child mutation after the snapshot. The row is finalized, but the signed artifact describes the pre-mutation state.
source_affected: All clinical child fields guarded by the trigger model, including blocks, modality entries and images; integrity attestations and corrections.
source_prerequisites: Two overlapping authenticated requests against the same draft session.
source_test_limitations: Existing tests cover concurrent finalizer-versus-finalizer calls, not finalizer-versus-child-write interleavings. Source tests cannot establish transaction ordering.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB integration test with two independent transactions and barriers: child mutation pauses after authorization, finalizer completes, child commit must block then fail; repeat for each child table and structured areas.
source_recommended_fix: Use a single per-session advisory/row-lock protocol for every clinical mutation and finalization. Commands that mutate children should lock the parent `FOR UPDATE` before checking draft status; finalization should acquire the same lock before collecting the snapshot.
source_rollout_considerations: Ship after the P0 guard or in the same containment series. Keep finalization disabled until the concurrency test passes from a fresh DB.

source_title: The signed finalization snapshot omits authoritative clinical fields added after the original design
source_evidence: The snapshot builder serializes a subset of session/block/entry/image fields. It does not include the authoritative `session_block_areas` rows and does not cover later probe-inventory linkage and conditional numbing fields introduced by migrations 0155/0156. A successful hash therefore is not a complete representation of the record visible to a practitioner.
source_failure_scenario: Two records with different structured areas, inventory-backed probe selection or numbing details can produce snapshots that do not reflect those differences. A verifier may report the hash as valid while important chart content has changed or was never represented.
source_affected: Finalized clinical records, legal/clinical exports, dispute resolution and future audit verification.
source_prerequisites: A finalized session containing any omitted field.
source_test_limitations: Tests that assert the existence of a hash or a selected JSON shape can pass while the shape is incomplete. A completeness contract against the current schema is missing.
source_acceptance_criteria: Golden DB tests create records differing one clinically meaningful field at a time and assert canonical snapshot/hash differences; verify round-trip rendering and export from the snapshot.
source_recommended_fix: Introduce a versioned canonical snapshot schema that includes every clinically authoritative table/field, sorted deterministically. Define explicit inclusion/exclusion rules and fail finalization if an unknown required schema version is encountered.
source_rollout_considerations: Do not mutate old snapshots. Store `snapshot_schema_version`; preserve legacy version verification and use attributed corrections/backfill attestations where needed.

source_title: Intake submission can overwrite a concurrent practitioner edit to the client profile
source_evidence: Submission uses a status compare-and-set for the intake, then separately reads the client, builds a patch from intake answers and updates the client by `id`. There is no version predicate, `updated_at` compare, field-level merge contract or transaction spanning submit and profile synchronization.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner corrects the client’s phone, birth date or other synchronized field while the client submits intake. The post-submit sync uses its earlier read and overwrites the newer practitioner value. Both actions appear successful.
source_affected: Client demographics/contact data and downstream appointment, consent and communication workflows.
source_prerequisites: Concurrent profile edit and intake submission affecting the same synchronized field.
source_test_limitations: The intake CAS test protects duplicate submission, not lost updates in the separate profile table. Ordinary unit mocks are unlikely to reproduce the interleaving.
source_acceptance_criteria: Two-connection DB test: update client after intake read but before sync; command must preserve the newer value or return a conflict requiring review.
source_recommended_fix: Move synchronization into a database command with explicit field authority and optimistic concurrency. Prefer storing intake answers as immutable submitted evidence and requiring a deliberate practitioner-reviewed merge for fields that can conflict.
source_rollout_considerations: Avoid silently re-running historical intake sync. Add a visible “profile differs from submitted intake” reconciliation state.

source_title: A draft intake can be marked reviewed without ever being submitted
source_evidence: The review action updates the intake to `reviewed` using intake ID and studio scope. It does not require current status `submitted`, verify that the intake belongs to the route client, check one affected row, or capture a submitted version as the reviewed artifact.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner opens a client route with a stale/mismatched intake ID or triggers the action before submission. The record becomes reviewed even though answers are incomplete or still editable, creating a false clinical review signal.
source_affected: Intake status, practitioner decision-making, audit records and any booking/treatment gate relying on “reviewed.”
source_prerequisites: Authenticated same-studio member and an intake identifier.
source_test_limitations: Happy-path UI tests may only exercise submitted intake. RLS membership prevents cross-studio access but not wrong-client or wrong-state transitions within a studio.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB tests for draft→reviewed rejection, wrong-client rejection, duplicate review idempotency and concurrent submit/review ordering.
source_recommended_fix: Implement a database transition command requiring `status = submitted`, matching `client_id`, active practitioner attribution, submitted version/hash and exactly one affected row. Make invalid transitions fail closed.
source_rollout_considerations: Existing erroneously reviewed rows require a safe audit/reconciliation report, not silent downgrade.

source_title: The owner export is described as complete but omits material clinical, privacy, payment and media records
source_evidence: The export reads a selected set of CSV datasets and explicitly excludes image binaries/storage paths and payment tables. It also omits intake/health forms, consent signatures/templates, clinical snapshots/corrections/amendments, portal messages and several audit/provenance tables. The UI says data is exportable and the README/action copy describes broad completeness.
source_failure_scenario: A studio leaves Hone, responds to an access request or needs a clinical/legal archive. The ZIP appears successful but lacks records required to reconstruct the full client history or verify finalized/corrected records. The studio may delete its account believing it has everything.
source_affected: Every studio/client, clinical/legal records, privacy requests and switching trust.
source_prerequisites: Owner runs the export and relies on its completeness.
source_test_limitations: Tests can assert expected filenames without comparing export coverage to the current schema/storage inventory.
source_acceptance_criteria: Seed one row/object in every exportable table/bucket; export, validate manifest/checksums and import into a verification tool. Test large studios and revoked/deleted records under retention policy.
source_recommended_fix: Define a versioned export manifest covering every tenant-owned table, consent/intake versions, snapshots/corrections, payment metadata, communication/audit records and image binaries with checksums. Generate a completeness report and allow independent validation.
source_rollout_considerations: Correct the UI immediately to say “partial export” until complete. Do not perform destructive offboarding based on the current artifact.

source_title: Quick Import is non-transactional and can strand clients without their treatment history
source_evidence: The action bulk-inserts clients, then inserts treatment-memory rows. If memory insertion fails, the clients remain while the batch is marked voided. A retry skips existing clients, so the original file may not repair the missing history. The final completed-state update result is also not checked.
source_failure_scenario: A large import succeeds for clients but fails on one malformed/history row or transient DB error. Operators see a failed batch, retry, and receive duplicate-skips while the client profiles remain permanently detached from expected treatment memories.
source_affected: Imported clients, historical treatment context, launch data quality and support workload.
source_prerequisites: Any failure after client insert and before all memory rows/final batch transition complete.
source_test_limitations: Happy-path import tests and per-row validation do not prove atomicity or idempotent recovery after a mid-batch fault.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection DB tests at every phase; retry same batch must converge to one correct result; cross-tenant IDs and spreadsheet formula payloads must fail safely.
source_recommended_fix: Implement a transactional import RPC or staged tables with validate→preview→commit. Give every source row stable identity, upsert idempotently, persist rejected rows and support safe resume/rollback.
source_rollout_considerations: Until fixed, require verified backups and post-import reconciliation; label workflow operator-assisted and do not use it as a self-serve launch dependency.

source_title: Any authenticated practitioner can choose an arbitrary session charge amount up to CAD 2,000
source_evidence: The action comments state the session price is a suggestion, accepts `amount_dollars` from the practitioner form, and permits any authenticated practitioner in the studio to initiate the charge. Stripe account, customer and payment method are server-derived, but amount authority is not owner-only or tied to an immutable invoice/service/session calculation.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner mistypes 500 instead of 50, manipulates the request, or intentionally charges an amount unrelated to the session. Idempotency can prevent duplicates but cannot make an unauthorized amount correct.
source_affected: Clients, studio funds, refunds/disputes and card-authorization evidence.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated practitioner, eligible saved card/session and live payments enabled.
source_test_limitations: Payment tests can verify amount reaches Stripe exactly as requested and still miss authorization policy. Owner-run claims are contradicted by the action.
source_acceptance_criteria: Action/DB/E2E tests reject member-supplied arbitrary values, altered hidden fields, wrong session/client/account and excessive deviations; verify receipts use the final authorized amount.
source_recommended_fix: Derive the default amount from server-authoritative services/session charges. Permit adjustments only to owners or an explicit role, with bounded reason codes, confirmation and audit. Consider dual confirmation above a threshold.
source_rollout_considerations: Before enabling another studio, reconcile existing charge attempts against expected service/session amounts and document the approved pricing authority.

source_title: Sentry can receive bearer credentials embedded in URL path segments
source_evidence: Request and breadcrumb scrubbing removes query strings but preserves path segments. Hone places high-entropy bearer credentials in the path. The generic regexes target emails, JWTs, Bearer headers and selected token-like formats; an opaque random path segment can survive. Error events or sampled traces can therefore transmit it to Sentry.
source_failure_scenario: An exception, failed fetch breadcrumb or sampled trace occurs on a token route. The event contains the raw path. Anyone with Sentry access—or a disclosure at that processor—may replay an unexpired intake, appointment-management, portal or calendar-feed credential.
source_affected: Client health/intake data, appointment controls, portal access and private calendar feeds.
source_prerequisites: Sentry enabled and an event/trace on a bearer-path route before token expiry/revocation.
source_test_limitations: Unit tests that scrub query parameters/JWTs may pass without opaque path-token cases. PostHog has a stronger route boundary, but Sentry does not inherit it.
source_acceptance_criteria: Sentry scrub tests with realistic opaque tokens in request URL, transaction, span description, breadcrumb and exception context; assert the token never appears in serialized event JSON.
source_recommended_fix: Canonicalize sensitive routes to templates before Sentry processing, e.g. `/intake/[token]`; drop transaction names/URLs/breadcrumb data for all bearer routes; add server-side allowlisted route metadata instead. Rotate/revoke credentials after suspected leakage.
source_rollout_considerations: Deploy scrub before enabling tracing broadly. Review Sentry retention/access and search historical events for route patterns without exporting raw tokens.

source_title: Availability, overrides, blockouts and service scheduling settings remain directly writable by any studio member
source_evidence: Early RLS grants full membership-scoped DML to schedule configuration tables. Later atomic/locked owner actions improve the intended path but do not remove the direct table capability.
source_failure_scenario: A non-owner practitioner or compromised member account edits another practitioner’s availability, removes blockouts, changes service settings or races a booking without the owner checks, locking and audit semantics in the newer actions.
source_affected: All practitioners and clients in a studio; booking reliability and operational trust.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated studio membership.
source_test_limitations: UI tests can confirm owner-only controls while direct PostgREST remains available. Negative grant/RLS tests are needed.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB tests assert members cannot modify another practitioner/studio-wide settings; approved commands serialize with public/internal booking.
source_recommended_fix: Revoke broad DML; separate owner-managed studio policy, practitioner self-availability and system materialization commands. Each command should lock the same capacity authority used by booking.
source_rollout_considerations: Coordinate with public-booking command migration so there is one consistent lock protocol.

source_title: Public booking ignores the practitioner-capacity emergency booking kill switch
source_evidence: Internal booking V2 locks the studio/capacity state and checks the booking-enabled control. Public booking inserts directly through the admin client after a slot recheck and never calls the authoritative command or the kill-switch check.
source_failure_scenario: An operator disables booking during a capacity incident or migration. Internal creation stops, but anonymous clients continue creating public appointments, defeating the emergency containment mechanism.
source_affected: Studio calendar, clients, practitioners and incident response.
source_prerequisites: A studio with public booking enabled while the capacity/system gate is disabled.
source_test_limitations: Tests limited to the internal command can pass. A cross-entry-point gate test is missing.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB/browser test toggles the kill switch between slot display and submit; submission must fail with a safe unavailable message and create no client/appointment side effects.
source_recommended_fix: Route all public appointment creation through a public-safe authoritative DB command that checks global/studio/practitioner gates under the capacity lock immediately before insert.
source_rollout_considerations: Ship before relying on the kill switch operationally or enabling multi-practitioner public booking.

source_title: Public booking is outside the capacity lock and can race schedule edits or authoritative internal commands
source_evidence: Public booking performs a slot recheck in application code and later inserts directly. It does not acquire the same studio/practitioner capacity lock used by internal booking and schedule writers, so the check and insert are not serialized with an availability change.
source_failure_scenario: A public slot is rechecked as available. At the same time, an owner saves an override/blockout or another command reserves capacity. The public insert commits based on stale policy. A unique overlap constraint may catch exact appointment overlap, but not all buffer, capacity, archive or policy races.
source_affected: Public clients, practitioner schedules, buffers and launch incident containment.
source_prerequisites: Concurrent public submit and schedule/capacity mutation.
source_test_limitations: Sequential tests and source assertions do not prove interleaving. Existing overlap tests may cover only hard appointment collision.
source_acceptance_criteria: Two-connection tests for public booking versus override, blockout, service archive, practitioner deactivation, internal booking and kill-switch toggle.
source_recommended_fix: Move public booking into the same DB transaction/lock protocol as internal creation; derive service duration and practitioner eligibility under lock; atomically create client/consent/appointment/audit or return no side effects.
source_rollout_considerations: Requires a compatibility wrapper for the anonymous/token surface; do not expose a broadly executable unsafe RPC.

source_title: DST conversion silently shifts nonexistent local times and cannot represent the second repeated hour
source_evidence: The helper explicitly documents that a Toronto spring-forward local time such as 02:30 maps one hour before the requested wall time, and a fall-back repeated 01:xx resolves to the first occurrence. Booking/move actions do not round-trip validate the selected wall time or expose an occurrence choice.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner enters 02:30 on spring-forward day and Hone records 01:30. On fall-back day, the second 01:30 cannot be selected. Reminders, calendar rendering, Google events and client expectations can disagree by an hour.
source_affected: Appointments near DST transitions in any supported timezone with gaps/overlaps.
source_prerequisites: Use of a nonexistent or ambiguous local time.
source_test_limitations: Existing tests may encode the current mapping as expected behaviour, creating false confidence rather than rejecting ambiguity.
source_acceptance_criteria: Unit and browser tests for Toronto/New York spring-forward and fall-back, midnight boundaries, long services and Google/notification rendering.
source_recommended_fix: Use a timezone library/API that detects nonexistent and ambiguous wall times. Reject gaps with a clear UI message. For overlaps, require/derive an explicit offset/occurrence and round-trip validate before writing.
source_rollout_considerations: Data audit for appointments created in transition windows; do not automatically shift historical rows without practitioner review.

source_title: A same-studio member can re-parent a draft clinical session to the wrong client through direct DML
source_evidence: Session and block policies are membership-scoped. The identity-freeze trigger protects selected session identity fields only after finalization. While draft, an authenticated studio member can update `client_id` directly if the row remains in the same studio.
source_failure_scenario: A buggy client, malicious practitioner or copied UUID changes a draft session from Client A to Client B. Existing blocks/entries now appear under the wrong client, potentially exposing sensitive history and causing future treatment decisions to use another person’s record.
source_affected: Client clinical histories, practitioner attribution, photos and treatment-memory views.
source_prerequisites: Same-studio membership and access to a draft session ID and another client ID.
source_test_limitations: Cross-tenant tests can pass because studio IDs remain correct. A same-tenant wrong-client negative test is required.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB tests reject direct client/studio/practitioner re-parenting in draft and finalized states; test approved command only under owner/authorized role with audit event.
source_recommended_fix: Freeze session identity from creation except through a dedicated audited reassignment command with strict no-child or explicit migration semantics. Revoke direct UPDATE on identity columns from authenticated users.
source_rollout_considerations: Audit existing sessions for identity changes where history permits. Avoid a blanket rewrite of affected records.

source_title: Broad authenticated appointment DML bypasses owner/member command authorization, invariants and audit
source_evidence: The appointment table is exposed under broad studio-membership DML while newer create/move commands implement role checks, capacity locks, authoritative duration and availability validation. A caller can bypass the newer command by calling PostgREST directly.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner changes duration, assignment, status or times directly, bypassing owner-only override rules, buffer semantics, kill switches and expected audit side effects. The database row may be valid structurally while violating scheduling policy.
source_affected: Appointments, practitioner calendars, client notifications, payment eligibility and audit history.
source_prerequisites: Authenticated studio membership and direct Supabase API access.
source_test_limitations: Server-action tests prove the command path, not that alternate table writes are impossible.
source_acceptance_criteria: Direct DML negative tests for every restricted field/status transition; command tests assert locks, authority, audit and one-row effects.
source_recommended_fix: Revoke authenticated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on appointments; expose narrow SECURITY DEFINER commands for create, move, cancel, complete, no-show and approved administrative repair. Use column privileges as an intermediate containment step.
source_rollout_considerations: Stage behind feature flags only if legacy clients require migration; instrument denied direct writes and provide an operator repair command.

source_title: SaaS subscription billing and entitlements are absent
source_evidence: Stripe Connect client payments are distinct from billing studios for Hone. There is no demonstrated plan subscription, dunning, entitlement, trial, cancellation, invoice/tax or access-suspension control plane.
source_failure_scenario: Paid acquisition requires manual invoicing and feature flags; failed payment does not map safely to access or data-retention state.
source_affected: Hone revenue operations and every paying studio.
source_prerequisites: Commercial rollout beyond founder-managed pilots.
source_test_limitations: Payment tests for client charges do not cover SaaS billing.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fake-provider subscription lifecycle tests including duplicate/out-of-order webhooks, dunning, plan changes and cancellation.
source_recommended_fix: After the safety pilot, build separate platform-billing customer/subscription/entitlement models with webhook idempotency, grace periods, manual override audit and no coupling to clinical data deletion.
source_rollout_considerations: Defer until studio #2 safety; required before scaling paid acquisition.

source_title: Calendar-feed bearer URLs lack rotation/revocation UI and last-used telemetry
source_evidence: The feed uses a high-entropy bearer URL, hash-only storage and generic busy content—good privacy foundations. The route comments defer a user-facing rotate/revoke capability, and no clear last-used telemetry is exposed.
source_failure_scenario: A feed URL is pasted into the wrong service, appears in logs or a device is lost. The owner cannot easily rotate it or see whether it is still used, so exposure persists until manual intervention/expiry policy.
source_affected: Practitioner availability privacy.
source_prerequisites: Token leakage or device change.
source_test_limitations: Route tests may validate hash and generic content but not lifecycle UX.
source_acceptance_criteria: Browser/route tests verify old token revocation, new token activation and no raw token in telemetry/Sentry.
source_recommended_fix: Add owner-controlled rotate/revoke, overlapping cutover window, last-used timestamp/client fingerprint minimization and alerts for unusual use.
source_rollout_considerations: Coordinate with F-PRIV-001 before broader feed use.

source_title: Hosting, encryption and compliance-facing UI claims are not fully supported by evidence in the ZIP
source_evidence: One settings surface says data is hosted in Canada and encrypted at rest, while the privacy page says Supabase infrastructure is in the United States and Canadian residency is being evaluated. The ZIP cannot prove cloud region, backup encryption, processor contracts or current deployment topology.
source_failure_scenario: A studio relies on the settings claim when deciding where sensitive data is stored. Contract/privacy representations conflict or become inaccurate as environments change.
source_affected: All studios/clients and commercial/legal trust.
source_prerequisites: Display of claims without environment-derived verification and legal review.
source_test_limitations: Marketing copy tests may assert wording rather than truth.
source_acceptance_criteria: Release gate checks a versioned claims manifest against environment/contract evidence; manual legal approval recorded.
source_recommended_fix: Reconcile every public/in-app claim to a signed infrastructure and subprocessor register. Use precise wording: operated from Canada is not the same as data residency in Canada. Obtain qualified privacy/legal review.
source_rollout_considerations: Correct contradictory text before additional sales; do not claim compliance broadly.

source_title: Whole-session-copy provenance can disappear through cascading deletes
source_evidence: The provenance ledger references source and target with `ON DELETE CASCADE`. Deleting either record can erase evidence that settings were copied, weakening historical attribution even though the copy itself is carefully designed.
source_failure_scenario: A session is deleted under an administrative/retention path. The ledger row disappears, and downstream reviewers can no longer see that another record originated from it.
source_affected: Copied session provenance and audits.
source_prerequisites: Deletion of source/target record.
source_test_limitations: Copy correctness tests may not exercise deletion/retention.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB test deletes/archives source/target and verifies provenance remains interpretable.
source_recommended_fix: Use durable tombstone identifiers or `ON DELETE RESTRICT/SET NULL` with immutable source fingerprint and human-readable provenance retained according to policy.
source_rollout_considerations: Coordinate with retention/legal-hold design.

source_title: Critical local verification lanes were environment-blocked
source_evidence: Dependencies could not be installed; the local shell is outside one locked dependency’s declared engine range; no local Supabase/browser stack was available. Typecheck, lint, build, unit, DB, browser, payment and Google lanes were not executed.
source_failure_scenario: Static defects remain valid, but regressions/build failures and behaviour covered only by tests remain unknown.
source_affected: Any launch decision based on “tests exist” or historical CI rather than exact-head execution.
source_prerequisites: Current audit limitation.
source_test_limitations: The required test lanes were not executed; this finding describes missing assurance rather than a failing code assertion.
source_acceptance_criteria: Exact-head CI artifact with all lane results and fresh-DB migration application.
source_recommended_fix: Run the exact archive/commit in hermetic Node 20.20+ CI with locked registry cache, local Supabase, Playwright and fake providers. Publish immutable logs and checksums.
source_rollout_considerations: This is a mandatory launch gate, not a request to weaken or edit tests.

source_title: Google Calendar “not registered” documentation is contradicted by Vercel cron configuration
source_evidence: `vercel.json` registers `/api/cron/calendar-reconcile` and `/api/cron/calendar-sync` on daily schedules. Some comments/docs describe those routes as not registered. The database claim path still appears to fail closed when `worker_enabled=false`, so registration alone does not prove provider calls.
source_failure_scenario: Operators assume no route invocation is possible and skip monitoring or secret configuration. Vercel invokes the routes; a future flag/config change activates work without the expected rollout awareness.
source_affected: Google-connected studios and operations.
source_prerequisites: Deployment uses this `vercel.json`; cron secret/routes configured.
source_test_limitations: Source tests may assert one document rather than reconcile deploy config and runtime flags.
source_acceptance_criteria: Config test enumerates registered cron routes and verifies each route’s fail-closed auth/global/studio/no-work behaviour.
source_recommended_fix: Make deploy configuration the source of truth, update docs, expose a runtime dormancy dashboard and require dual global+studio gates plus zero-work metrics.
source_rollout_considerations: No Google enablement until deploy config, flags, secrets and operator checklist reconcile.

source_title: Google refresh-token key rotation has no dual-key window and requires reconnect on key change
source_evidence: Ciphertext is versioned and AES-GCM fail-closed, which is good. The runtime exposes only the active key; a version mismatch makes the connection reconnect-required rather than decrypting with a previous key and rewrapping.
source_failure_scenario: Routine key rotation or accidental key replacement disconnects every active studio at once. Operators must coordinate reconnects, creating calendar drift and support load.
source_affected: All Google-connected studios.
source_prerequisites: Key rotation with existing encrypted secrets.
source_test_limitations: Crypto unit tests can validate fail-closed behaviour without proving safe fleet rotation.
source_acceptance_criteria: Rotation test with mixed key versions, concurrent refresh and rollback; no plaintext logging.
source_recommended_fix: Support current+previous key IDs or KMS envelope encryption, rewrap secrets under controlled jobs, monitor completion and retire old keys after verification.
source_rollout_considerations: Design before broad Google rollout; current reconnect posture may be acceptable for a tiny controlled pilot if documented.

source_title: Inbound busy-time import and true two-way Google Calendar synchronization are not built
source_evidence: The archive supports connection and outbound-sync foundations. It does not establish inbound busy-time ingestion or conflict-aware two-way synchronization. Marketing/roadmap language must preserve that distinction.
source_failure_scenario: A practitioner assumes personal Google events block Hone availability, but Hone continues offering the slot, or assumes Google edits flow back when they do not.
source_affected: Google-connected practitioners/clients.
source_prerequisites: Expectation of two-way sync.
source_test_limitations: Outbound fake-provider tests do not prove inbound semantics.
source_acceptance_criteria: Future provider-contract tests for recurrence, timezone, deletion, rate limits and conflict reconciliation.
source_recommended_fix: Keep scope labeled outbound-only. Validate whether inbound busy import is truly required; if built, define source of truth, privacy, recurrence, deletion and conflict policy first.
source_rollout_considerations: Defer until outbound reliability and real demand are proven.

source_title: No complete offboarding, studio deletion and provider-disconnection workflow exists
source_evidence: The archive lacks one controlled workflow that freezes writes, creates/verifies a complete export, handles retention/legal hold, revokes tokens, disconnects Google/Stripe, resolves storage, schedules deletion and records approvals.
source_failure_scenario: A studio leaves and Sam must improvise SQL/provider steps. Data may be deleted prematurely, retained indefinitely or leave active integrations behind.
source_affected: All studios, clients and providers.
source_prerequisites: Cancellation/offboarding request.
source_test_limitations: Feature-level tests do not cover lifecycle orchestration.
source_acceptance_criteria: End-to-end sandbox offboarding test including retry/rollback and post-delete access denial.
source_recommended_fix: Design a state machine with owner/admin approvals, export checksum, retention clock, provider revocation, legal hold, deletion jobs and final certificate.
source_rollout_considerations: Required before contractual self-serve cancellation or 10 studios.

source_title: Studio provisioning creates only the studio and owner invitation; onboarding remains operator-assisted
source_evidence: The action performs two core service-role writes and compensates if the invitation fails. It does not provision a complete service catalogue, availability, intake/consent defaults, policies, provider state, payment fee controls, practitioners or launch verification.
source_failure_scenario: Studio #2 is created successfully but cannot safely operate until Sam performs one-off configuration and checks across many screens or production data.
source_affected: New studios and founder support capacity.
source_prerequisites: Every onboarding.
source_test_limitations: Studio-create tests do not prove launch readiness.
source_acceptance_criteria: Provision from empty state twice, interrupt each step and verify resume/rollback; produce launch manifest.
source_recommended_fix: Create a versioned provisioning template and idempotent launch workflow with defaults, explicit choices, validation, recovery and evidence. Avoid hidden production SQL.
source_rollout_considerations: Founder-led assistance is acceptable to 10 studios, but the process must be repeatable and auditable.

source_title: Onboarding declares readiness after only service, availability and public-booking checks
source_evidence: Only three steps are required for `requiredComplete`; payments are optional and many safety/operational prerequisites are absent: privacy terms, consent/intake review, practitioner roles, export test, reminders, incident contact, provider flags, training and launch verification.
source_failure_scenario: The UI reports a studio ready while critical controls or legal/clinical setup are incomplete, creating false confidence for founder and studio owner.
source_affected: New studio launch.
source_prerequisites: Completion of the current three steps.
source_test_limitations: Tests may faithfully assert the inadequate checklist.
source_acceptance_criteria: Onboarding tests ensure no studio reaches launched state with any mandatory gate missing; operator override requires reason/audit/expiry.
source_recommended_fix: Separate “booking configured” from “production launch approved.” Add a versioned launch gate with mandatory safety, data, provider, training and support evidence.
source_rollout_considerations: Use manual approval for 0–10 studios; automate only after the checklist is proven.

source_title: Public rate limiting intentionally fails open during limiter/provider failure
source_evidence: The contract explicitly allows public slot, booking and token-route requests when the limiter backend errors. This prioritizes availability but removes abuse containment precisely during provider/configuration failure.
source_failure_scenario: A Redis/Upstash outage or missing environment value allows unrestricted slot scans, booking attempts or token endpoint traffic. Attackers can amplify DB/provider load or nuisance bookings.
source_affected: Public endpoints, database/provider capacity and studio operations.
source_prerequisites: Limiter failure plus abusive traffic.
source_test_limitations: Unit tests may correctly assert fail-open semantics without evaluating operational impact.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection load tests with limiter unavailable; ensure mutation throughput remains bounded and legitimate read traffic has a controlled degraded path.
source_recommended_fix: Use endpoint-specific posture: local bounded fallback, stricter fail-closed/degraded mode for mutation/token verification, circuit breakers and per-studio/IP/device signals. Return privacy-safe errors.
source_rollout_considerations: Coordinate with public booking atomicity and abuse monitoring.

source_title: Twilio STOP handling scans every phone-bearing client across studios in one service-role process
source_evidence: Twilio signature verification is strong. After verification, the route uses service role to fetch phone-bearing clients broadly, normalizes/filter matches in application memory, then applies a deliberate global phone-wide opt-out across studios.
source_failure_scenario: As data grows, one inbound STOP performs a large cross-tenant PII read in a single process. A logging/debugging mistake or memory/latency failure affects many studios; shared/recycled phone numbers can opt out unrelated records.
source_affected: Client phone data and messaging consent across all studios.
source_prerequisites: Valid signed inbound STOP and matching/reused number.
source_test_limitations: Signature tests do not prove query scalability or cross-tenant privacy minimization.
source_acceptance_criteria: DB tests for multiple studios/shared numbers, indexed query plan and no PII returned to route beyond affected IDs/counts.
source_recommended_fix: Store normalized phone hashes/indexes and execute a narrow audited DB command. Preserve legally required global opt-out semantics only after privacy/legal confirmation, with minimal returned data and explicit provenance.
source_rollout_considerations: Migrate normalized hashes before volume grows; document consent semantics.

source_title: Appointment reminders depend on an external scheduler with no Vercel cron registration in the archive
source_evidence: The reminder route exists but `vercel.json` registers recurring breaks and Google jobs, not appointment reminders. Documentation may rely on an external scheduler, but the ZIP cannot prove it exists, is authenticated, runs at the required cadence or has heartbeat monitoring.
source_failure_scenario: The external schedule is removed, misconfigured or delayed. Reminders silently stop while the application remains healthy.
source_affected: All studios using reminders and their clients.
source_prerequisites: Missing/failing external scheduler.
source_test_limitations: Route tests cannot prove the job is invoked in production.
source_acceptance_criteria: Staging job test plus production no-op heartbeat verification; simulate missed schedule and recovery without duplicates.
source_recommended_fix: Make scheduler ownership explicit, register it in deploy-as-code or an independently attested provider, add heartbeat/lag metrics and alert on missed windows.
source_rollout_considerations: Mandatory launch evidence for each studio using reminders.

source_title: No backup restore drill, RPO/RTO, on-call or incident-command evidence is included
source_evidence: The ZIP contains alerts/runbook material but no immutable evidence of backup configuration, restore success, recovery point/objective, incident ownership, escalation or rollback rehearsal.
source_failure_scenario: A database/storage/provider incident occurs and recovery depends on ad hoc production queries and founder memory.
source_affected: All studios and data.
source_prerequisites: Production incident.
source_test_limitations: Unit tests cannot prove restoration or human response.
source_acceptance_criteria: Restore a sanitized environment from backup, verify tenant/data/object counts and run core workflows; record signed results.
source_recommended_fix: Define RPO/RTO, backup scope including storage, quarterly restore drills, incident roles, communication templates, kill switches and deployment rollback evidence.
source_rollout_considerations: Mandatory before 10 studios and repeated before 50/100.

source_title: Operational alerts have no durable retry and can be lost on database/email failure
source_evidence: The helper redacts and attempts logging, DB insertion and critical email, but deliberately does not throw. A failed alert insert/send is logged and dropped without an outbox or retry.
source_failure_scenario: The system encounters the exact provider/database failure that should create an alert; alert persistence or email also fails, leaving no durable incident signal.
source_affected: Operations and affected studios.
source_prerequisites: Alert-path dependency failure.
source_test_limitations: Happy-path alert tests do not prove delivery under failure.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection tests for DB, email and logging failures; at least one independent signal must remain observable.
source_recommended_fix: Use a durable local/outbox path where possible, provider-independent fallback metrics and heartbeat monitoring. Track delivery state/retries without exposing PII.
source_rollout_considerations: Avoid recursive alert storms; define bounded retry/dead-letter behaviour.

source_title: Public booking deposits, card collection, packages and partial payments are not built or deliberately held
source_evidence: The public booking flow does not collect a card/deposit. Packages, split/partial payments and a complete fee lifecycle are absent or held. This is safer than prematurely enabling them, but limits commercial parity.
source_failure_scenario: Studios expecting deposits/no-show protection must use another tool or manual process.
source_affected: Studios requiring these payment models.
source_prerequisites: Feature demand.
source_test_limitations: Not applicable.
source_acceptance_criteria: Future provider-contract/E2E tests with amount, consent, cancellation and refund invariants.
source_recommended_fix: Do not build until public booking authority, consent and amount logic are safe. Validate demand and legal/card-authorization wording before implementation.
source_rollout_considerations: Explicitly defer during P0/P1 remediation.

source_title: Public-booking audit duplicates raw email and free-text notes
source_evidence: The booking audit payload stores raw email and notes in addition to the canonical client/appointment records. Free text may contain sensitive details and duplicates expand access, retention and breach scope.
source_failure_scenario: A client enters health-adjacent information in notes. It is retained in both appointment/client surfaces and audit JSON, where deletion/export policies may differ.
source_affected: Public-booking clients and audit readers.
source_prerequisites: Any booking with email/notes.
source_test_limitations: Audit-event existence tests often reward richer payloads without checking minimization.
source_acceptance_criteria: Tests assert raw email, phone and arbitrary notes never appear in audit/log/ops payloads.
source_recommended_fix: Store stable IDs, normalized event metadata and a redacted/hash representation; keep sensitive content only in its canonical protected record. Define audit retention separately.
source_rollout_considerations: Migrate or redact historical audit payloads only under an approved retention plan.

source_title: Repository provenance is incomplete because the ZIP contains no Git metadata
source_evidence: The archive comment contains a SHA-like value, but branch, commit ancestry, dirty/untracked state, submodules and whether the tree exactly equals that commit cannot be established.
source_failure_scenario: A stale, locally modified or selectively packaged tree is reviewed as though it were production. Findings may be fixed already or missing from the deployed branch.
source_affected: Audit accuracy and release decision-making.
source_prerequisites: Reliance on the ZIP as exact production source.
source_test_limitations: No code test can restore missing provenance.
source_acceptance_criteria: CI attestation compares archive tree hash to checked-out commit and records artifact digest.
source_recommended_fix: Future audits should use an immutable Git archive generated by CI with commit, tree hash, lockfile hash, migration manifest, build provenance and deployment ID.
source_rollout_considerations: Treat every deployment/merge claim in this report as unverified until reconciled.

source_title: Public booking is non-transactional and can leave client/consent side effects when appointment creation fails
source_evidence: Client creation or consent updates occur before the direct appointment insert. Appointment collision/failure can return an error after those earlier mutations have committed. Marketing consent and audit/provider side effects occur in later stages as well.
source_failure_scenario: Two clients race for a slot or the appointment insert fails. A new client record remains even though no appointment exists, or consent/profile state changes from an unsuccessful booking attempt.
source_affected: Client directory, consent state, deduplication and support workflows.
source_prerequisites: Failure after client/consent mutation.
source_test_limitations: Happy-path browser tests and appointment uniqueness checks do not prove all-or-nothing semantics.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection and race tests assert zero durable side effects on every rejected submit.
source_recommended_fix: Create a single public-booking DB command that validates and atomically creates/reuses client, records consent evidence, inserts appointment and audit row. Dispatch email/SMS from an outbox after commit.
source_rollout_considerations: Provide a cleanup/reconciliation report for orphan clients created by failed booking attempts.

source_title: Knowing an existing client email permits nuisance bookings against that client record
source_evidence: The existing-client branch normalizes email and reuses a matching client without authenticating control of the address. This is common in low-friction booking, but it permits impersonation/nuisance bookings and can mutate selected consent fields.
source_failure_scenario: Someone who knows a client’s email books unwanted appointments, consuming capacity and attaching bookings to the existing profile. No private data need be disclosed for operational harm to occur.
source_affected: Existing clients and studio calendar.
source_prerequisites: Knowledge of studio slug, email and an available slot.
source_test_limitations: Functional tests may intentionally accept this flow; abuse tests are needed.
source_acceptance_criteria: Browser tests for known-email impersonation, repeated nuisance submissions, rate-limiter outage and confirmation expiry.
source_recommended_fix: Choose an explicit risk posture: email verification/magic link for recognized clients, confirmation before high-impact bookings, anti-abuse scoring and non-mutating consent handling. Preserve accessible first-time booking.
source_rollout_considerations: Validate with studio workflow; classify as accepted limitation only with controls and disclosure.

source_title: Retention, deletion, legal hold and complete studio purge are not implemented as a coherent process
source_evidence: Policies discuss retention, but code evidence does not show a complete schedule that applies consistently to database rows, audit logs, snapshots, storage objects, provider data, backups and legal holds.
source_failure_scenario: A deletion/access request or contract termination is handled inconsistently. Some sensitive data persists while provenance needed for legal/clinical reasons is removed, or vice versa.
source_affected: All personal/clinical data.
source_prerequisites: Retention/deletion request or elapsed policy window.
source_test_limitations: Table-level delete tests cannot prove cross-system lifecycle.
source_acceptance_criteria: Sandbox lifecycle test across DB, storage, providers and export; backup deletion limitations explicitly documented.
source_recommended_fix: Create a data inventory with purpose, legal basis, retention, deletion/anonymization and hold rules; implement idempotent jobs and evidence reports with qualified legal/privacy review.
source_rollout_considerations: Required before self-serve deletion and broader regulated-jurisdiction sales.

source_title: Studio export is unbounded, built fully in memory and duplicated as base64
source_evidence: The action loads all selected rows, creates the entire ZIP in server memory and converts it to base64 for return through a server action. Binary expansion and duplicate buffers increase memory significantly.
source_failure_scenario: A studio with years of data causes high memory use, timeout or process termination. The export fails exactly when portability matters most, and retries repeat the full load.
source_affected: Larger studios and serverless capacity.
source_prerequisites: Large row counts/files.
source_test_limitations: Small fixture tests do not model memory/timeout behaviour.
source_acceptance_criteria: Load test at projected 100k clients/1m records and large image corpus; enforce quotas and cancellation.
source_recommended_fix: Generate exports asynchronously with paginated/streamed reads, object storage, manifest/checksums, expiry and resumable status. Stream download rather than base64 server-action payload.
source_rollout_considerations: Pair with complete-export redesign rather than optimizing the incomplete format.

source_title: “Next available” scans dates sequentially and can multiply database work per request
source_evidence: The action loops day by day up to its horizon and invokes slot generation repeatedly. Each day can issue several DB reads. Sparse calendars and public abuse can multiply latency and load.
source_failure_scenario: A studio has no availability for weeks. One anonymous request performs many sequential queries; concurrent users amplify load and tie up serverless execution.
source_affected: Public booking and database capacity.
source_prerequisites: Sparse availability or abuse.
source_test_limitations: Unit tests on a few dates do not measure query count/latency.
source_acceptance_criteria: Benchmark sparse/dense calendars at 10/50/100 studios and assert maximum query/time budget.
source_recommended_fix: Query/materialize candidate availability in bounded ranges, cache safe schedule inputs, paginate search and enforce a request work budget with metrics.
source_rollout_considerations: Address before paid traffic; do not optimize ahead of correctness/atomicity.

source_title: Public multi-practitioner booking is not implemented safely; appointments resolve to owner or null
source_evidence: The public action looks up the studio owner and assigns that practitioner (or null). It does not expose a validated practitioner choice, no-preference allocation or capacity-aware assignment.
source_failure_scenario: A multi-practitioner studio publishes booking expecting team availability. Public appointments land on the owner or unassigned, distorting capacity and requiring manual repair.
source_affected: Studios with more than one practitioner and their clients.
source_prerequisites: Multi-practitioner public launch.
source_test_limitations: Schema/capacity tests do not establish public allocation behaviour.
source_acceptance_criteria: Browser/DB tests for chosen practitioner, no preference, parallel practitioners, deactivation, reassignment and cross-studio practitioner substitution.
source_recommended_fix: Add explicit service-practitioner eligibility, practitioner choice/no-preference policy and atomic assignment under the capacity lock. Do not infer readiness from schema alone.
source_rollout_considerations: Keep public multi-practitioner disabled until a controlled pilot passes.

source_title: Slot generation ignores several database query errors and can return misleading availability
source_evidence: Blockout, capacity/default and reservation queries consume `.data` without consistently surfacing `.error`. A failed query can be interpreted as no blockouts/reservations or missing defaults rather than an unavailable scheduling service.
source_failure_scenario: A transient DB/RLS/query error omits a conflict input. Hone shows a slot that should be blocked, or returns an empty/misleading calendar with no operational alert.
source_affected: Public/internal availability and clients.
source_prerequisites: Any relevant query error.
source_test_limitations: Mocks that return data only do not exercise error branches.
source_acceptance_criteria: Unit tests inject each query error; public submit must revalidate and create no booking; UI distinguishes “no availability” from system failure.
source_recommended_fix: Fail closed for mutation-relevant availability, return a distinct temporary-unavailable state, emit redacted ops metrics and avoid caching incomplete results.
source_rollout_considerations: Ship with public atomic command; do not expose provider/database details.

source_title: No staging, canary rollout or migration-rehearsal evidence is included
source_evidence: The repository has local test intent and production gate scripts, but the ZIP cannot establish a production-like staging environment, canary process, migration rehearsal against realistic data or rollback evidence.
source_failure_scenario: A migration/feature passes local tests but fails on production data shape, provider configuration or scale. All studios receive it at once.
source_affected: Production-wide releases.
source_prerequisites: Any nontrivial deployment.
source_test_limitations: CI source tests cannot establish staged rollout.
source_acceptance_criteria: Rehearse P0 snapshot migration and public-booking command on representative data before production.
source_recommended_fix: Create sanitized production-shape staging, migration dry-run/rehearsal, feature-flag canary by studio, automated smoke tests and rollback/forward-fix decision records.
source_rollout_considerations: Required before 10–50 studio growth.

source_title: Treatment-image upload can leave orphaned private objects when metadata insertion and cleanup both fail
source_evidence: The action uploads the object first, then inserts metadata. On metadata failure it attempts deletion and emits an alert if cleanup fails. There is no durable reconciliation queue or periodic orphan scanner shown.
source_failure_scenario: Storage upload succeeds, DB insert fails, and cleanup fails transiently. The object remains private but untracked, cannot be exported through metadata and may persist indefinitely.
source_affected: Client images, retention obligations and storage cost.
source_prerequisites: Cross-system partial failure.
source_test_limitations: Mocked cleanup tests cannot prove eventual reconciliation.
source_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection tests for every failure point and reconciler convergence without cross-tenant deletion.
source_recommended_fix: Create a durable upload intent/object ledger and reconciler; use deterministic state transitions, checksums and retention-safe quarantine. Periodically compare bucket objects to metadata.
source_rollout_considerations: Do not expose orphan paths; preserve incident/audit evidence.

source_title: A large source-string assertion surface creates false confidence about runtime behaviour
source_evidence: Source/migration shape tests are useful guardrails, but many assert that strings, comments, function names or fragments exist. They cannot prove RLS under real roles, transaction isolation, provider request semantics or UI behaviour.
source_failure_scenario: A refactor can preserve asserted text while behaviour is unsafe, or safe behaviour can break tests because formatting changes. Passing counts may be presented as stronger evidence than they are.
source_affected: All critical workflows and release decisions.
source_prerequisites: Reliance on aggregate test count without coverage classification.
source_test_limitations: This finding is about evidence quality, not a claim that all source tests are bad. The local DB harness is a strong counterexample.
source_acceptance_criteria: Coverage map must identify the behavioural layer for every P0/P1 regression and fail releases that have source-only coverage.
source_recommended_fix: Label test classes in CI; shift highest-risk assertions to DB/browser/concurrency/provider-contract behaviour; retain source guards only for truly static invariants.
source_rollout_considerations: Incremental conversion; do not delete guards until stronger tests exist.

source_title: Critical concurrency regressions are missing for finalizer-vs-child-write and public-booking-vs-schedule mutation
source_evidence: The suite covers selected duplicate/finalizer cases and hard-overlap scenarios, but the two confirmed races do not have two-connection barrier tests that reproduce their transaction ordering.
source_failure_scenario: A future change passes all ordinary tests while preserving or reintroducing a signed-snapshot mismatch or stale public-booking commit.
source_affected: Clinical records and booking reliability.
source_prerequisites: Concurrent requests.
source_test_limitations: Sequential browser/unit tests cannot establish serialization.
source_acceptance_criteria: The regression itself is the required evidence: old code must fail, fixed code must pass reliably across repeated runs.
source_recommended_fix: Add deterministic two-connection DB tests with synchronization barriers and repeat under relevant isolation levels. Test every entry point against the same lock authority.
source_rollout_considerations: Run in mandatory DB CI, not an optional slow lane.

source_title: Mobile Chromium coverage is not physical iOS Safari or accessibility acceptance evidence
source_evidence: The repository has a mobile browser lane, but emulated/Chromium behaviour cannot prove WebKit/Safari quirks, physical keyboard/viewport behaviour, camera/photo flows, screen-reader semantics or practitioner usability on real devices.
source_failure_scenario: A flow passes CI but fails in Chloe’s actual iPhone/Safari workflow or is too slow/confusing during treatment.
source_affected: Practitioners and clients on mobile.
source_prerequisites: Device/browser-specific behaviour.
source_test_limitations: Playwright remains valuable; it is simply not equivalent to physical acceptance.
source_acceptance_criteria: Acceptance checklist: calendar, booking, intake, charting, photo upload, copy, finalization/correction and payment.
source_recommended_fix: Add WebKit CI, automated accessibility checks and a short recorded acceptance script on target physical devices for launch-critical flows.
source_rollout_considerations: Do not describe Chromium emulation as iOS proof.

source_title: Export audit metadata omits four generated record-keeping filenames
source_evidence: The export constructs additional record-keeping CSVs, but the audit metadata’s listed files do not include all generated files. The artifact and audit event can disagree about what was produced.
source_failure_scenario: An operator later relies on the audit event to determine export contents and receives an incomplete list.
source_affected: Owner/auditor.
source_prerequisites: Any export containing those files.
source_test_limitations: Filename tests can miss metadata parity.
source_acceptance_criteria: Test manifest, archive entries and audit payload are exactly equal.
source_recommended_fix: Generate audit file list directly from the manifest used to build the archive.
source_rollout_considerations: Fold into complete-export redesign.

source_title: Selected comments and documents state production/deployment facts that the source cannot prove
source_evidence: Several documents assert hosted migration maxima, deployed state or route registration. Some older migration comments still say “NOT hosted-applied,” while newer docs say all are applied; Google route-registration language conflicts with `vercel.json`.
source_failure_scenario: Reviewers/operators use a stale statement as an operational control or skip verification.
source_affected: Engineering and operations.
source_prerequisites: Documentation drift.
source_test_limitations: Documentation tests often assert text, not truth.
source_acceptance_criteria: Release job fails when migration manifest/deploy config differs from generated docs.
source_recommended_fix: Maintain one generated deployment/capability register from CI/deployment/provider evidence. Mark historical comments as historical rather than authoritative.
source_rollout_considerations: Do not rewrite migration history merely to update comments; reconcile in current docs. --- # PART 5 — SECURITY, MULTI-TENANCY AND PRIVACY
